### Scaffold
Place an app's bar, navigation rail, pane and trailing toolbar.

Component ID: `scaffold`

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/scaffold.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/scaffold.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.18.1)

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `css-only`. [Google guidance](https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/scaffold/overview)

Example: A mail app with an app bar, a navigation rail, a scrolling inbox and a trailing toolbar of side apps uses a scaffold. The list and message inside the inbox use list-detail panes.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: pattern. Layout foundation pattern; the scaffold positions existing components and adds none of its own.

Upstream: requirements-prose-reviewed (2026-11-15); [evidence](https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/scaffold/overview).

Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

Support (2026-11-15, `llm.md#scaffold`): A window-height grid that places a header app bar across the top and a navigation rail, main and vertical toolbar below it, with region classes for custom content and only the pane scrolling. A tall-rail modifier runs the rail and trailing region the full height with the bar over the pane. From 600px to 839px an expanded rail opens over the pane with a scrim. Below 600px the document scrolls, with the app bar and a bottom navigation bar pinned and the rail hidden until it opens as an overlay. A trailing vertical toolbar floats there as a centered row above the navigation bar. A status bar takes a full-width row along the bottom from 600px up. From 600px up a navigation bar stays in a row of its own when no rail is shown. From 600px up the pane floats as a rounded surface on a surface-container shell. From 1200px up an open standard side sheet becomes a third column. With viewport-fit=cover its regions stay inside the safe areas.

Web adaptation: CSS grid areas on a div inside body; the children keep their own landmarks, and the app bar's scrolled fill reads the pane's scroll through timeline-scope.

Known boundary: Region placement, pane-only scrolling, the rail's fill and expansion, the trailing toolbar's position, panes inside main, RTL, the app bar's pane-scroll fill, enlarged text, print, keyboard scrolling and landmark order are checked in a browser, and so are the compact layout's document scrolling, pinned bars, hidden rail and 600px boundary, and the floating compact toolbar's row, placement, tooltips and scroll padding, and the status bar's row and compact hiding, and the floating pane's colors, corners and gaps, and the side sheet column; the safe-area insets are checked with rewritten env() values; spoken output, a real notch and a mobile browser's collapsing address bar remain unverified.

Full parity remains unassessed. [Capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#scaffold).

#### Contract

Places an app shell's bar, navigation rail, pane and trailing toolbar, so a page needs no shell grid of its own.

Put `.scaffold` on a `<div>` that is a child of `<body>`. Not on `<body>` itself: the browser moves the body's overflow to the viewport, and the shell stops clipping. Its direct children are placed by component: a `<header>` top app bar spans the top, and a `.navigation-rail`, `<main>` and a `.toolbar.vertical` (or `.toolbar-group.vertical`) share the row below it, from the leading edge to the trailing one. From 600px up the scaffold is as tall as the window (`100dvh`) and only `<main>` scrolls; a rail with more destinations than fit scrolls them itself. The components keep their own look and behavior. The scaffold itself is CSS only; there is no scaffold JavaScript component. The app bar's menu button toggles the rail when its `aria-controls` names the rail's `id`, once `AutoInit()` has started the rail.

#### Syntax

```html
<div class="scaffold">
  <header>
    <a class="visually-hidden-focusable" href="#main">Skip to content</a>
    <div class="bar">
      <button type="button" aria-label="Main menu" aria-controls="rail" aria-expanded="false">
        <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">menu</span>
      </button>
      <h1>Mail</h1>
    </div>
  </header>
  <nav class="navigation-rail" id="rail" aria-label="Primary">
    <a href="/inbox" aria-current="page"><span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">inbox</span>Inbox</a>
    <a href="/starred"><span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">star</span>Starred</a>
  </nav>
  <main id="main" tabindex="-1">…</main>
  <div class="toolbar vertical">
    <button type="button" aria-label="Calendar"><span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">calendar_month</span></button>
  </div>
</div>
```

#### Rules

- `scaffold-is-not-a-landmark`: Write the scaffold as a <div> inside <body>. Its header, navigation rail and main are the landmarks; a role on the scaffold would wrap them in another one.
- `scaffold-one-child-per-region`: Each scaffold region holds one visible child: one header or .scaffold-bar, one navigation rail or .scaffold-rail, one main or .scaffold-pane, one vertical toolbar or .scaffold-trailing, one .status-bar, and one direct-child navigation bar. A second one lands in the same grid area and overlaps the first. Add hidden to the ones not shown; hidden="until-found" still takes part in layout, so it counts as shown.
- `scaffold-does-not-nest`: A scaffold is as tall as the window and holds the page's one main, so it can't sit inside another. Use panes or the grid inside the scaffold's main.

#### Guide checks

- Label every <nav> landmark with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
